summary: Owner feedback round on n150, part 1 of 3 (brief 14a via relayed delegation; items 2, 3, 4, 7 of 8). Root cause found for both flash reports: FS_ABYSS displayed base + dye.rgb with no clamp while vortex() injected 0.35 dye per frame, so the leave/dive vortex saturated channels to white and bloomed — the 'supernova' at dive end and the white flash on Surface. Fix: hue-preserving soft shoulder in FS_ABYSS (linear to 0.55, asymptotic 0.82 max-channel) + soft accumulation ceiling in FS_SPLAT_DYE (knee 2.6, ceil 4.0, uniform scale so the ink-mode black-dye rule survives); vortex dye 0.35 to 0.12/frame; dive tangential ramp 40+120t. Lantern spring retuned near-critical (desktop k32/c10.6, touch k40/c12, vmax 1500, thrust 1100) for the 'moves too fast/erratic' verdict. Wake trail rebuilt: stroke now takes css px/s (hysteresis gate 120/70), momentum fraction 0.16, smoothstep dye ramp 0.05..0.20 over 90-800 px/s — continuous plume, no dots, no cliff. Dive iris inverted: hue now GROWS to full cover (linear 1s, flat colour from ~0.77s) so the SPA cut lands under the signature colour. Integrator deviation: wakeOn moved from module scope into the scene closure (the brief's FIND block placed it module-scope, shared across instances). Gates: tsc strict OK, vite build OK, realm-probe 18/18 behavioural (2 console errors are fonts.googleapis.com ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT — this Windows network, unrelated), realm-shots inspected: flood cover intact, wake reads as a continuous warm plume, no white clipping anywhere.
